pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered fully and customised to his shift pattern — 'the two days you're home, you're going to hit a 30 to 40-minute workout, and the two days you're gone, you're not' — plus five to ten minutes of daily mobility to counteract twelve-hour sitting. The prospect tied it straight back to his own diagnosis of the problem: 'I think that that's a very clear picture of it. And as you said before, and it's true, I think that's what I've been missing... to put all of that together. And so I can apply my consistency because I have the discipline.' He then volunteered a long unprompted statement of readiness — 'I think I'm tailor-made for this kind of thing. This is why I'm here.'

Presented with the LA-to-New-York train-track analogy and a no-macro-tracking promise. The prospect volunteered a positive reaction and connected it to his own plateau: 'it always appeals to me when somebody says, Jerry, we're going to show you how to eat sensibly, to get the results you want, and you don't have to measure anything, you just need to be satiated so you can feel balanced and strong, so you can attack this thing that you want to, this plateau you're trying to reach... I like that. I like that idea.' Notable that he already owns 'all the scales, food scales, smart scales' and has tried tracking.

Delivered in full — weekly check-in form, Trevor's cell number, chase messages for missed workouts, the community, and the lifelong-success framing 'in six months, we want to teach you everything that you need to know to have this be sustainable for the rest of your life... By the end of this, you don't need us anymore.' The prospect said 'Yes' and 'that's good to know' but gave no substantive reaction — he pivoted immediately into talking about his overweight 30-year-old son. Unlike the first two pillars the rep did not ask 'what's your thoughts on that?' here, so no real reaction was ever collected on the pillar that most directly answers his stated problem.

anchors.raw: And I really have told them the same thing. And what it is, is it's cross-training. So I have the feeling that kettlebells would serve me better. And you guys are really in the same ballpark in terms of time and finance.
anchors.note: Rare shape: a competitor anchor that validates the price level rather than attacking it. $6,000 was never contested because a comparable coach had already quoted him something similar and he had spoken to them earlier the same day. The threat this anchor creates is entirely on provider choice, not on cost — 'It's not the commitment or the program or the money... Who do we go with?'. Worth noting that the rep, having never met a same-price competitor in the script, responded by moving price anyway.

anchors.raw: You know, I was, I was thinking five. I had my wife speculating, you know, they're going to want about five grand, you know? Yeah. So that sounds really in the ballpark of where I figured you guys are going to be at.
anchors.note: He and his wife had independently pre-framed the price at roughly $5,000 before the call. $6,000 landed inside their expected range and drew no resistance whatsoever — the word 'okay' twice and then a move to the next topic. Evidence that the $6,000 number is well-calibrated for this segment, and evidence that the $1,200 concession offered twenty minutes later was unnecessary.

anchors.raw: This was my ego. This was my insane, insatiable thirst to try to find a resolution to my problem... damn, have you ever noticed how much stuff you have that's built on pulling up, pushing and pulling from the point of pull-ups and dips?
anchors.note: He has already spent heavily on kettlebells, weighted ropes, a hip sled, calisthenic rings and Parabody equipment, and frames that spending as a failed search for the answer. A prospect who has already paid this much for equipment that did not solve it is pre-sold on paying for the missing piece. The rep used this well — 'you already have the kettlebells, you already have all this stuff' — but did not use it as a price justification.

unmet_demand.want: Help fixing his sleep. He named it as the single biggest blocker — 'I think sleep is a critical point and I have to get better sleep because I think without that factor, nothing works' — and separately disclosed sleep apnea, five to five and a half hours a night, and a family history of insomnia. He is already self-medicating with valerian root, ashwagandha and magnesium.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Sleep appears in none of the three pillars. The rep asked about it in baseline, heard it named as the number one root cause, and then presented training/mobility, nutrition and accountability without mentioning sleep once. It was never addressed again in the offer, the delivery walkthrough or the commitment check.

unmet_demand.want: Recovery management appropriate to a 70-year-old — he explicitly identified under-recovery, not under-effort, as his failure mode: 'I was working myself beyond the ability to recover. Without recovery, you have no progression.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme almost certainly does programme recovery and deloads, but nothing in the presentation said so. The closest the rep came was the accountability pillar's 'he's going to be like, no, no, hang out. It's okay. You don't have to stress. Trust the process', which addresses his impatience but not the physiology.

unmet_demand.want: Pelvic floor rehabilitation after prostate removal and radiation. This is a stated purchase driver, not an aside: 'what I do is try to use kettlebells in a way that help me emphasize developing strength in my core, absolutely first and foremost, but also my pelvic floor... once again, what attracts me to kettlebells is the core development of the movements and the fact that I'll strengthen my pelvic floor.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never acknowledged. The rep did not respond to the pelvic floor or the incontinence at any point in the call, and the training/mobility pillar made no reference to it. The prospect is buying partly on a therapeutic belief about what kettlebell work will do for a post-prostatectomy pelvic floor, and nobody either confirmed, qualified or corrected that belief.

unmet_demand.want: Individualisation for a 70-year-old body specifically — 'nothing is cookie cutter. I have to effectively be able to make this work for me as an individual', and a fear of being turned away for his age.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partly served. The rep did address it directly with the coached-guys-in-their-70s-and-80s proof point and the custom-programming promise, which is the right answer. Left here as unvalidated rather than resolved because the specific adaptations an ex-cancer, post-surgical 70-year-old would need were never described, and the claim 'you will get results, and you will feel 10 times better than 95% of the 70-year-olds out there' was asserted rather than substantiated.
